description: The most recent reported value of each metric for one ticker. Pass as_of to get the snapshot as it stood on that date — only filings public by then are considered, so an answer for that date uses nothing published later. Tickers look like AAPL, 2330.TW, 005930.KS, 0403091220.BE, 775670417.FR, CC21860.NZC. Suffixes are not all listed equities, and not all figures mean what the column name suggests. .TW income-statement values are SINGLE-QUARTER (three-month) amounts: Taiwan files cumulative year-to-date totals and they are converted before you see them, so do NOT difference adjacent quarters again. A .TW row with fp FY is the full-year total, not a quarter. .TW current quarters come from the TWSE OpenAPI (Open Government Data License v1.0, attribution required); history from 2013 comes from the TWSE MOPS XBRL archive, which is NOT open data: keep both attribution notices and do not call Taiwan figures open data. US figures (SEC EDGAR) are public information. .TW filing dates are the statutory reporting deadline, a deliberately late proxy, not the actual release date. .BE is Belgian STATUTORY SOLO accounts, never group consolidation. .NZC is New Zealand REGISTERED CHARITIES (Charities Register annual returns), not listed companies. .FR is INPI's register of keyed-in annual accounts: `filed` is dateDepot, the register's own deposit date, and balance sheets are included. Coverage is substantially complete from 2022; 2017-2021 is still backfilling. Turnover is lawfully absent from roughly 36% of French deposits (confidentiality declarations); it is PRESENT on 64.0% of company-periods, and the API's /api/v1/fundamentals/quality endpoint reports the measured share of every metric in every market. The reporting model rides in `form` (K consolidated, C complet, S simplifie); consolidated and own accounts are separate deposits with their own dates, so both can appear for one SIREN and period. .DK is similar: its filing dates are the register's REAL publication timestamps, and turnover is present on only 10.5% of company-periods (Belgium is lower still at 8.1%) because Danish reporting class B may publish gross profit instead — that absence is lawful disclosure, not missing data, and gross profit is never a substitute for it. A .DK `form` is annual (Danish GAAP) or annual/ifrs, with the period's length appended when a year is not 11-13 months (annual/15m for a long first year); interim reports are excluded.
name: get_latest_fundamentals
title: Latest fundamentals for a company
